name: Telemagenta
lede: Telemagenta is a strong purplish red from the German RAL color system, used for signage and almost never seen in painting.

sections.title: A signal color
sections.body:
RAL, the German industrial color standard founded in 1927, lists Telemagenta as RAL 4010, and the hex value here is a screen approximation of that spec [1]. Wikipedia independently cites the same RAL entry, with no earlier source for the name [1]. The books consulted give no account of why it is named for telecommunications rather than any other field, so that origin is undocumented here [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in our library is [[red-purple]], a slightly less pink, more violet hue [1]. The app's own closest common-name match is [[mulberry]], about 5.8 units away [1]. RAL also lists a second reddish-purple signal color, [[traffic-purple]], deeper and less pink than Telemagenta but from the same 1927 standard [1]; that color in turn sits near [[flirt]] in our library [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this exact hue, as photographed, in only 1 of 23,781 paintings, rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [2]. A strong, saturated magenta this close to a modern industrial standard is almost never a match for old pigments, so the single hit is likely a late or restored work rather than a historical dye [2]. Beyond that single painting, the sample is too small for century, painter or company statistics [2].
